question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees get?
expected_answer: 28 days a year, including bank holidays (more with long service, up to 30).
ai_answer: Full-time employees get 28 days of paid annual leave each leave year, including bank holidays, under the Annual Leave Policy (§4). Long-service days are added on top: 1 extra day after 3 years' continuous service (29 days in total) and 2 extra days after 5 years (30 days in total), with a maximum entitlement of 30 days. The Employee Handbook (§6) also states 28 days, plus extra days for long service, and refers to the Annual Leave Policy for booking rules.

question: When do we get paid?
expected_answer: Monthly, on the last working day of the month.
ai_answer: Employees are paid monthly on the last working day of the month, according to the Employee Handbook §5 Pay. Payslips are available in StaffHub.

question: How long is the probation period for new starters?
expected_answer: 6 months, with reviews at 3 and 6 months; can be extended by up to 3 months.
ai_answer: New employees have a 6-month probation period. Their manager holds review meetings at 3 months and 6 months, and probation may be extended by up to 3 months if more time is needed.

question: What is the mileage rate if I use my own car for work?
expected_answer: 45p per mile (normal commuting can't be claimed).
ai_answer: Mileage in a personal car is paid at 45p per mile under the Expenses Policy (v2025.1, §3). Normal commuting to your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

question: How long does my password need to be?
expected_answer: At least 14 characters, with MFA wherever supported.
ai_answer: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long, according to section 4 of the Information Security Policy (v2025.1). The IT Acceptable Use Policy (section 7) confirms employees must follow these same password rules.

question: How quickly must a customer complaint be acknowledged?
expected_answer: Within 2 working days (final response within 8 weeks).
ai_answer: A customer complaint must be acknowledged within 2 working days, according to the Customer Complaints Procedure (v2025.1, effective 1 Jun 2025), §5 Timescales. The final response is due within 8 weeks.

question: How much company sick pay do I get if I've worked here for 4 years?
expected_answer: 4 weeks at full pay in any rolling 12 months (after probation), on top of SSP.
ai_answer: If you have between 3 and 5 years' service and have completed probation, you get 4 weeks of company sick pay at full pay in any rolling 12-month period. Company sick pay tops up SSP to your full basic pay.

question: What support can I get for studying a qualification?
expected_answer: Course fees up to £1,000 a year and up to 5 days' paid study leave, after probation.
ai_answer: Once you have passed probation, you can apply for study support for a qualification relevant to your role. It covers course fees of up to £1,000 per year and up to 5 days of paid study leave per year for exams and study. Applications are made through LearnHub and must be approved by your line manager and the Head of Learning and Development. If you leave within 12 months of a course finishing you must repay 100% of the course fees, and if you leave 12 to 24 months after it finishes you must repay 50%.

question: If I leave 18 months after the company paid for my course, do I have to pay anything back?
expected_answer: Yes, 50% of the course fees (leaving between 12 and 24 months after the course).
ai_answer: Yes. Under the Training and Development Policy, if you leave between 12 and 24 months after your course finishes, you must repay 50% of the course fees. Leaving 18 months after the course finished falls in this band. The policy refers to the date the course finishes, not the date the company paid, so if your course ended later than the payment date, the timing would run from the finish date. The passages do not state how the repayment amount is calculated or collected.

question: Is there an allowance for working from home?
expected_answer: £26 a month for employees contracted to work remotely at least 1 day a week.
ai_answer: Yes. Employees whose contract says they work remotely at least 1 day a week receive a home working allowance of £26 a month, paid through payroll (Remote and Workplace Policy v2025.1, §4). The passages do not say anything about allowances for employees whose contracts do not include remote working.

question: Can I roll over unused holiday into next year?
expected_answer: Yes, up to 8 days, which must be used by 30 June.
ai_answer: Yes, you can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year, and you do not need approval to do so. Carried-forward days must be used by 30 June of the new leave year, otherwise they are lost and not paid. The days appear automatically in StaffHub from 2 January. The Annual Leave Policy (§5) is the source for these rules; the Handbook (§6) confirms that the carry-forward rules sit in that policy. The passages do not say what happens to any unused days beyond the 8-day limit.

question: I clicked a dodgy link in an email. What should I do?
expected_answer: Report it to the IT Service Desk immediately (and use Report Phish for suspicious emails).
ai_answer: If you have already clicked a link in a suspicious email, report it to the IT Service Desk immediately. You should also report the suspicious email using the Report Phish button in Outlook, and do not click any further links or open attachments in it.

question: Can I keep the tips a punter gives me at the blackjack table?
expected_answer: No. Gaming staff tips go in the tronc box and are shared through the tronc scheme.
ai_answer: No. Gaming employees must never keep tips personally. Tips given to gaming employees are placed in the tronc box at the table and shared through the tronc scheme (Code of Conduct §3). Hospitality employees follow their venue's tipping process instead.

question: I'm too poorly to work my shift on the casino floor. How early do I need to ring in?
expected_answer: At least 2 hours before the shift starts, by phone to the line manager or duty manager.
ai_answer: Gaming floor employees must phone their line manager or the duty manager at least 2 hours before the start of their shift so cover can be arranged, and must call again each day they are absent unless their manager agrees otherwise or they have a fit note. Do not text or email unless you cannot speak.

question: How quickly do I have to report a lost company laptop?
expected_answer: Immediately, and in any case within 1 hour, to the IT Service Desk.
ai_answer: A lost or stolen company device, including a laptop, must be reported to the IT Service Desk immediately, and in any case within 1 hour of noticing it is missing.

question: What happens to my annual leave if I'm ill while I'm on holiday?
expected_answer: With a fit note, those days count as sickness and the leave is given back. Report it on day one.
ai_answer: If you are ill during booked annual leave and provide a fit note covering the days of sickness, those days are treated as sickness absence and the annual leave is returned to you. You must report the sickness on the first day, following section 2 of the Sickness Absence Policy. The passages do not say how to submit the fit note or what happens if no fit note is provided.

question: Where do I report a customer I think is laundering money?
expected_answer: Directly to the MLRO with the internal suspicious activity report form, not SafeLog; never tell the customer.
ai_answer: Do not report it in SafeLog. Report it directly to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) using the internal suspicious activity report form, and send it on the same day. Do not investigate yourself and do not tell the customer, as tipping off is a criminal offence.

question: Can I claim my course fees back on expenses?
expected_answer: No. Course fees are paid directly by the company under the Training Policy.
ai_answer: No. Course fees cannot be claimed on expenses. Under the Training and Development Policy (§6), course fees are paid directly by the company, and the Expenses Policy (§6) lists training course fees among the items that cannot be claimed. Travel and accommodation for approved training can be claimed under the Expenses Policy.

question: Someone on the gaming floor looks under 18. What do I do?
expected_answer: Ask for photo ID (Think 25), tell the duty manager immediately, and log it before the end of the shift.
ai_answer: Nobody under 18 may enter the gaming floor, so someone who looks under 18 must not be allowed onto it. Under the Think 25 rule, anyone who appears to be under 25 must show valid photo ID. The passages do not say what to do if the person is already on the floor or refuses to show ID, so check with your duty manager on those points.

question: I was off sick for months last year and couldn't use my leave. How much can I carry over and by when?
expected_answer: Up to 20 days because of long-term sickness, to be used within 18 months of the end of that leave year.
ai_answer: Because your absence was long-term sickness, you may carry forward up to 20 days under the exception in §8 of the Annual Leave Policy, rather than the standard 8 days. Days carried forward because of sickness must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which they were earned. The policies do not say how this applies to your specific leave years, and the 20-day exception also requires that the carry-forward is an exception you qualify for under §8; the standard §5 rule (8 days, used by 30 June) applies otherwise.

question: Can gaming floor staff take two weeks off over Christmas?
expected_answer: No. 24 Dec to 1 Jan is a peak period; at most 5 consecutive days, and only with the General Manager's approval.
ai_answer: Not as a single block of two weeks. The 24 December to 1 January period is a peak period, and gaming floor and security employees may take no more than 5 consecutive days of leave during peak periods, and only with approval from their venue's General Manager. Leave must also be requested through StaffHub with notice of at least twice the length of the leave (so 2 weeks of leave needs about 4 weeks' notice). Gaming floor rotas are published 4 weeks in advance, and requests made after publication can only be approved if cover is available. The passages do not say whether leave could be split into separate blocks over Christmas beyond the 5-consecutive-day limit.

question: How much notice do I need to give to book a week of annual leave?
expected_answer: Twice the length of the leave, so 10 days for 5 days of leave; later if the rota is already published.
ai_answer: You must give notice of at least twice the length of the leave requested, so for a week (7 days) of leave you need to request it at least 14 days before the first day of leave. Requests must be made through StaffHub. Note that if the gaming floor or security rota has already been published (4 weeks in advance), a request made after publication can only be approved if cover is available. Managers should respond within 5 working days.

question: How much annual leave can I carry forward?
expected_answer: Up to 8 days, used by 30 June (the 2024 rule of 5 days by 31 March no longer applies).
ai_answer: You can carry forward up to 8 days of unused annual leave into the next leave year without needing approval, and these must be used by 30 June of the new leave year or they are lost and not paid. In limited exceptions, up to 20 days may be carried forward where leave could not be taken because of long-term sickness, maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, or where a manager cancelled approved leave for business reasons and the Head of People approved the exception in writing. Sickness-related carry-forward must be used within 18 months of the end of the leave year in which it was earned; other exceptional carry-forward must be used by 30 June.

question: How many days a week can office staff work from home?
expected_answer: Up to 2 days with manager agreement; Tuesday and Wednesday are office days (not 3, as in 2023).
ai_answer: Employees in office-based support roles (such as Finance, HR, IT, Compliance and Marketing) may work remotely for up to 2 days a week, with their line manager's agreement. Tuesday and Wednesday are anchor days, when office-based employees are expected to be in the office unless they are on leave or have agreed otherwise with their manager.

question: Am I allowed to work from abroad for a few days?
expected_answer: Office-based staff can, for up to 10 working days a year, with manager and Information Security approval in advance.
ai_answer: Yes, but only within limits. Employees in office-based support roles may work from outside the UK for up to 10 working days in a calendar year. Each trip must be approved in advance by your line manager and by the Information Security team, and the request must be made through the IT Service Desk at least 2 weeks before travel. The policies do not say what happens if a request is made with less notice or what the process is for requests beyond 10 days.

question: How long does the MLRO have to decide whether to report a suspicious activity report to the NCA?

ai_answer: The MLRO must decide within 5 working days of receiving the internal SAR whether to submit an external Suspicious Activity Report to the National Crime Agency through SAR Online. The reasons for the decision must be recorded in every case, including when no report is made.
